spec: Rule cards for libretro cores whose save behaviour deviates from RetroArch's standard savefile_directory rule. This is world knowledge under DESIGN.md's boundary rule: each card states WHICH live config governs the core and what its values mean — the current value is always read from the machine, never from here. A card states only what no read of the machine recovers: the .so name is derived from the card key and never restated, an option default is recorded only for a core that registers none (a probe of the binary reads the others), and what a card does state about the core's own vocabulary is machine-checked wherever a machine can check it. Cards are keyed by the core's canonical short name (the .so basename without _libretro.so, matching libretro-core-info filenames); 'identifiers' carries the display library_name the core binary reports, the one name that key does not give. 'saves.anchors' is that vocabulary's tripwire: every file name and subdir fragment a card records is pinned either to 'literal' — the whole NUL-delimited byte string the auditor read in the shipped .so, which a test re-reads there — or to an explicit reason no literal can carry it ('unprotected', the core composes the name at run time; 'arrangement', the path is one the arrangement builds and not the core's word at all). A recorded name with neither fails the tests; there is no silent opt-out. Facts live here; interpretation lives in code — a rule that does not fit this schema gets code plus a card referencing it, the schema does not grow a DSL. A declared file name may carry the placement's own hole tokens and nothing else (<rom_stem>, which the resolver fills from the content path, and <save_id>, which it never fills and hands to the caller as a hole); the loader refuses any other token, so a typo cannot travel into a filename atlas states as fact. A subdir segment may be exactly one of the placement's subdir templates — <rom_stem>, or <content_dir_name>, the basename of the content's directory — whole-segment only (the resolver's segment arithmetic depends on one template filling to one segment) and only under the savefile_directory root; the resolver fills it from the content path, and a content-less question keeps the token in the path with its hole in needs. A mode may state 'inside_content' instead of 'groups': no separate save file exists — the loaded content file itself takes the writes (quasi88 with its option on). The value is the reason, required prose; the root must be content_directory, and the answer becomes a declared emptiness with the save-inside-content caveat carrying the fact — never the content file presented as a save under a second name. Its harder sibling is 'writes_discarded': nothing keeps a save at all (hatari with write protection on discards the changed image at eject; SwanStation with both card slots on none) — same construction, its own save-writes-discarded caveat, granularity 'none', and the two statements refuse to ride one mode together; it may also anchor at savefile_directory, where the writes would have landed. A card whose modes no single option's value can name states 'governing_rule' instead of 'governing_option': the options its selection rule reads (possibly none), with the rule itself registered in atlas.mode_rules under the card key — freely named modes, the card states what can exist and the rule decides what holds here. A mode whose every group is unnamed states the directory and refuses the names (ScummVM's launcher-target slot files); its declared set is the empty set of statable names and never claims completeness. The other closed vocabularies are the placement's too: 'root' is savefile_directory | system_directory | content_directory | working_directory (working_directory is the launch's own directory — the answer stays a <cwd> template with its hole in needs). A group may anchor at another root than its mode ('root' on the group, issue #97 — the retired 'also_under' field's successor, which now fails the load): established only from a savefile_directory mode into system_directory or content_directory, never the first group, always with files — the part reaches the caller as a FileGroup where the set is declared and always as a file-set-spans-roots caveat naming the resolved directory and files, 'granularity' is shared-card | shared-file | per-game-file | per-game-files | per-game-directory, and 'complete' must be a JSON boolean — never a quoted one, which Python would read as true. Format and per-field rules: atlas/data/README.md, in the repository.

This core takes itself out of the libretro save interface deliberately and says so above the two functions: 'there is no safe/sensible way to use the memory interface without severe hackery. provenance.source:
Cannonball source at the revision the shipped binary names, which reports only 'git' as its library_version, so the pin is that build. retro_get_memory_size returns 0 for every id (src/main/libretro/main.c:1128-1131), so RetroArch writes no save file. The core builds three paths of its own at load: retro_build_save_paths joins the frontend's save directory to 'hiscores', 'hiscores_timetrial' and 'hiscores_continuous' (:945-971), and Config_save_scores and its siblings write them through config_open_write, which appends '.sav' to whatever it is handed (src/main/frontend/config.c:75-81, :181-216). The comment above the three joins warns that they are not full paths — the suffix is added elsewhere — which is exactly what that append is.

All three are one group because they are one directory and one meaning: three score tables for the game's three modes. They are shared-file rather than per-game because nothing in the name follows the content — this core runs one arcade game, and a second copy of that game's data would write the same three files. That makes it the first shipped card whose whole save is a score table, and the reason the high-score role exists: a client merging two devices takes the higher entries here rather than the newer file.

Where the frontend hands over no save directory the core falls back to the content's own directory (:957-959), which is the same fallback the standard rule already has.

The core answers RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM with 8 KiB while it is in CD mode and 0 otherwise (libretro.c:1497-1518, its data twin at :1478-1495), and CD mode follows the content's own file extension — '.chd' or '.cue' turn it on (:1205-1218). The stem is the content's basename with its last extension cut (:313-320), and the save directory comes from GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY (:1326-1327).

The second name is the reason this core needed a card rather than a record, and it is worth stating plainly: for CD content the core writes <rom_stem>.srm at unload AND RetroArch writes <rom_stem>.srm for the memory id the core just filled. For cartridge content there is no collision at all: the id is empty, RetroArch writes nothing, and the four files are the core's alone.

provenance.source: Virtual Jaguar source at 48096c1, the revision the shipped binary names in its library_version. On load the core takes GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY into vjs.EEPROMPath and the content's basename into vjs.romName (libretro.c:883-895), and builds two paths from them: <save_dir>/<rom_stem>.srm for the cartridge EEPROM and <save_dir>/<rom_stem>.cdrom.srm for the JagCD one (eeprom.c:99-109). Both are written whenever the game writes its EEPROM — the state machine calls EEPROMSave on a word write and on a write-all with writes enabled (eeprom.c:148-167, reached from :299-308 and :336-344), which is the ordinary in-game save rather than a shutdown path. The core also answers RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM with the same 128 bytes (libretro.c:958-965), so RetroArch writes <rom_stem>.srm as well: one path, two writers, and not the same bytes — the core stores the words as big-endian pairs (eeprom.c:42-53, mirrored by its reader at :57-65) while the frontend writes the memory block raw. Which one a file ends up holding depends on who wrote last; that is an emulator question, and it is stated here because a client comparing two machines' files will meet it. Two conditions the file names cannot carry: content whose CRC32 is 0xFDF37F47 — the Memory Track device — is exempt and gets no EEPROM files at all (eeprom.c:90-96), and content loaded without a path falls back to naming both files after the ROM's CRC32 (<CRC32>.srm, <CRC32>.cdrom.srm, eeprom.c:106-108); no launcher on either arrangement is known to load Jaguar content that way.

Slot 1 is always the frontend's: the card reaches RetroArch through the SRAM interface and the standard <content stem>.srm is written by RetroArch itself (frontend/libretro.c:2050-2068, :3483-3496). 'pcsx_rearmed_memcard2' — the core's only save option, registered disabled/enabled with 'disabled' as the default (frontend/libretro_core_options.h:152-165) — adds the core-written pcsx-card2.mcd beside it, one second-slot card shared by every game (frontend/libretro.c:3500-3525). No per-game spelling exists for the second slot, so the two modes are the whole space and one option's values select them.
